$about: Glowing embers rising from a hot surface. Data only — no functions, no asset paths. Unknown keys are ignored; invalid values fall back to the defaults in config.ts and are reported in the console.
$emission: The source area sits at emissionHeight above the effect's own origin — position risingembers.object3d on the hot surface itself. Width and depth are full extents. emissionRate is embers per second; the live population settles at rate x average lifetime and is capped by particleCount, so the rate sets the density and the count sets the budget.
$motion: riseSpeed is the average over a life, not the launch speed: the climb eases out as the ember cools. driftSpeed is a coherent wind every ember shares, spread is the cone the column opens into, turbulence is the per-ember wander. maxHeight caps the travel so a long-lived ember cannot leave the shot.
$look: The three colours are one temperature ramp, coolColor -> baseColor -> hotColor. Each ember is born somewhere on it and slides down as it ages, and the draw is biased low: most embers live in the dim red half and only a few reach hotColor and carry a white centre. Sizes are world units, minScreenSize is a floor in screen space (fraction of viewport height) that stops the far ones going sub-pixel. sizeVariation is how far size is allowed to come loose from heat.
$life: Lifetimes in seconds; hotter embers live toward the top of the range. fadeOutDuration is long on purpose — an ember should go out, not switch off. coolingIntensity drives both the colour slide toward coolColor and the dimming that goes with it.
